ideas.name: Monthly Forward Discount Carry
ideas.claim: Sort currencies by their one-month forward discounts and hold the highest-interest-rate portfolio long and the lowest-interest-rate portfolio short.
ideas.quote: The fifth panel reports returns on zero-cost strategies that go long in the high interest rate portfolio and short in the low interest rate portfolio.

rules.market: Currencies against the US dollar, including developed currencies; the full sample also includes emerging-market currencies.
rules.entry: At month-end, sort currencies into six groups by one-month forward discount; go long the highest-interest-rate group and short the lowest.
rules.exit: After one month, settle the forward positions against spot and rebalance.
rules.filters: Availability of spot and forward rates; specified observations with large failures of covered interest parity are excluded.

ideas.claimed_result: The paper reports an annualized Sharpe ratio of 0.32 for the developed-country long-short strategy. For the broader sample, it reports a 4.54 percentage point annualized net return and a 0.50 Sharpe ratio after bid-ask spreads, over the reported 1983–2009 sample.
required_data: Historical currency spot bid and ask rates
Historical one-month forward bid and ask rates
